{{essay-like|date=February 2021}}
'''Measurement dysfunction''' describes a situation or behavior where actual data metrics, statistics and especially their meaning (or communicated meaning), can become problematic due to misuse.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Presentations and Papers|url=http://www.osel.co.uk/presentations.htm|access-date=2021-02-22|website=www.osel.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|last=Austin|first=Robert D.|title=Measuring and managing performance in organizations|date=1996|publisher=Dorset House Publishing|others=Tom DeMarco, Timothy R. Lister|isbn=0-932633-36-6|location=New York|oclc=34798037}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Measurement Dysfunction|url=https://proactsafety.com/blog-posts/measurement-dysfunction|access-date=2021-02-22|website=proactsafety.com}}</ref> Specifically, in areas such as human resources (performance measurements),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Measurement Madness: Recognizing and Avoiding the Pitfalls of Performance Measurement {{!}} Wiley|url=https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Measurement+Madness%3A+Recognizing+and+Avoiding+the+Pitfalls+of+Performance+Measurement-p-9781119970705|access-date=2021-02-22|website=Wiley.com|language=en-us}}</ref> technology (safety),<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Vincent|first=Charles|title=The measurement and monitoring of safety : drawing together academic evidence and practical experience to produce a framework for safety measurement and monitoring|date=2013|others=Susan Burnett, Jane Carthey|isbn=978-1-906461-44-7|publisher=The Health Foundation |location=London|oclc=861644942}}</ref> finance or health,<ref name=":1" /> measurement dysfunctionality is critical, as it can lead to negative outcomes, wrong predictions or forecasts.

Practices to avoid:<ref>{{Cite web|title=When Measurement Goes Bad|url=https://www.amanet.org//articles/when-measurement-goes-bad/|access-date=2021-02-22|website=www.amanet.org|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

* Reward of wrong behavior (also persons who manipulate<ref>{{Cite web|title=How to Spot and Stop Manipulators|url=http://www.psychologytoday.com/blog/communication-success/201406/how-spot-and-stop-manipulators|access-date=2021-02-22|website=Psychology Today|language=en-US}}</ref>)
* Measuring the wrong things<ref>{{Citation|last=Leonelli|first=Sabina|title=Scientific Research and Big Data|date=2020|url=https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/sum2020/entries/science-big-data/|encyclopedia=The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy|editor-last=Zalta|editor-first=Edward N.|edition=Summer 2020|publisher=Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University|access-date=2021-02-22}}</ref>
* Measuring either not enough or too much
* Cheating or data manipulation (intentional or unintentional due to wrong calculation models, systematic errors, human errors, etc.)
On eliminating dysfunctional measurement:<ref>{{Cite web|last=Shelley|first=C. C.|date=October 2009|title=eXtreme Measurement: recognizing, understanding and avoiding measurement dysfunction|url=http://www.osel.co.uk/presentations/XMslides.pdf|access-date=2021-02-22|website=www.osel.co.uk|publisher=Oxford Software Engineering}}</ref>

* Establish, and monitor the move to and adherence to ‘policies’ for good, functional measurement
* Support technical correctness
* Periodically evaluate the information need and value delivered by measurements
